statement: d07 started with the ocentra-enforcer coordination MCP hub unavailable (same persistent hub-down condition already logged by e01/d06 in this build window). Per protocol (log+proceed), d07 proceeded without a ledger claim or a 'd07 started' mail attempt succeeding, and built its owned files (crates/enforcer-coordination/src/fix_loop.rs, src/fix_loop/dispatch.rs, tests/fix_loop.rs, tests/fixtures/fix_loop/**) directly on lane/d07.
why: Confirms the hub-down condition spans this lane too; an orchestrator or hub-repair task should check git log on lane/d07 directly rather than the coordination ledger for this lane's claim/lifecycle history.
howToApply: Check git log on lane/d07 directly rather than the coordination ledger.

statement: run_fix_loop's accept gate is a re-scan-and-compare, never a trust of FixGenerator::attempt_fix's own return value: acceptance requires BOTH findings_after < findings_before AND no new RuleId appears versus the pre-attempt RuleId set (IterationReason::NewRuleIdIntroduced rejects a count-decreasing edit that smuggled in a different rule violation -- the workpack's 'strictly decrease AND no new RuleId' is a conjunction, not an either/or, and this is enforced in code, not just asserted in a doc comment). A dedicated test (a_generator_that_lies_about_changing_anything_is_still_gated_by_rescan) uses a FixGenerator that returns Ok(true) while writing nothing, to prove the gate is the re-scan, not the generator's self-report.
why: Matches the enforcer doctrine elsewhere (rules proven by re-running the validator, not by asking the model/generator); a future fix-generator implementation that lies about having improved something must still be caught.
howToApply: Any new FixGenerator impl (crates/enforcer-coordination/src/fix_loop/dispatch.rs) should assume its return value is only a hint to the loop about whether to keep iterating, never a claim the loop trusts for accept/revert.

statement: The workpack's checklist item 5 ('logged as a d04 telemetry record via the enforcer-core NDJSON sink') is only PARTIALLY landed: run_fix_loop emits a typed FixLoopDecisionEvent (implements enforcer_events::event::DomainEvent, event_kind == 'coordination.fix_loop.decision') via an on_decision: impl FnMut(&FixLoopDecisionEvent) callback, but this module does NOT itself open an enforcer_core::telemetry::RunTelemetrySink and write NDJSON lines. Reason: the workpack's own stated caller (enforcer-cli's fix command, d06) has not landed a live oracle entry point on rust-build yet -- d06's own proof row and memory stream (mem-d06-0002) document fix_oracle() as failing closed with FailReason::NotYetWired precisely because d07 (this workpack) had not landed when d06 ran. Wiring on_decision to RunTelemetrySink<FixLoopDecisionEvent> is a one-line addition at whatever call site eventually drives fix_oracle's real implementation.
why: Avoids either (a) silently skipping the telemetry requirement or (b) inventing a telemetry sink this module cannot yet exercise against a real caller -- the deferred-wiring seam is documented explicitly in proof/rules/d07-fixloop.txt and the workpack's own checklist rather than silently marked done.
howToApply: When wiring enforcer-cli's fix command to a real oracle, call enforcer_coordination::fix_loop::run_fix_loop with an on_decision closure that appends each FixLoopDecisionEvent to a RunTelemetrySink<FixLoopDecisionEvent> opened at enforcer_core::telemetry::default_run_telemetry_path() (or the fix-loop-specific path convention chosen at that time).

statement: Confirms mem-d06-0003's lesson from a second lane: the workspace clippy deny wall (unwrap_used/expect_used = deny) applies uniformly to #[cfg(test)] modules inside src/*.rs AND to standalone tests/*.rs integration binaries -- cargo clippy -p enforcer-coordination --all-targets -- -D warnings failed on multiple `"RR-7.1".parse().expect(...)` and `"a.txt".parse().expect(...)` calls in both fix_loop.rs's #[cfg(test)] module and tests/fix_loop.rs, even though the harness.rs crate (enforcer-validator) elsewhere models the correct pattern (`.parse()?` inside a `-> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>>` test fn). Also hit clippy::redundant_clone twice from `rule_id: rule_id.clone()` when rule_id was never used again after constructing the struct.
why: A worker who copies the .expect()-based test-fixture-construction idiom from an example elsewhere in the codebase without checking clippy --all-targets will get a lint failure that looks unrelated to their actual logic change.
howToApply: Every test helper that builds a RuleId/RelPath/etc from a string literal via .parse() must live in a fn returning Result<T, ...> and propagate with `?`, never .expect()/.unwrap() -- in both src/*.rs #[cfg(test)] modules and tests/*.rs integration files. Before constructing a struct field with `x.clone()`, check whether `x` is used again afterward; if not, move it in directly.
